title: 2 Kings Chapter 4 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Kings chapter 4 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Kings Chapter 4 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Kings Chapter 4.

questions.question: Who came to Elisha crying for help because her husband had died?
options: A certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets
A widow from Shunem
The great woman of Shunem
A woman from Baalshalisha
questions.correctAnswer: A certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 4:1 states that a certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets cried unto Elisha because her husband was dead.

questions.question: What did the woman say her husband feared?
options: The LORD
Man's laws
The king
The creditor
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 4:1 says the woman’s husband did fear the LORD.

questions.question: What was the creditor threatening to take from the woman?
options: Her two sons to be bondmen
Her house
Her pot of oil
Her livestock
questions.correctAnswer: Her two sons to be bondmen
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 4:1 explains the creditor came to take her two sons as bondmen.

questions.question: What did Elisha ask the woman when she came to him for help?
options: What hast thou in the house?
How many sons do you have?
Have you prayed to the LORD?
Where is your husband?
questions.correctAnswer: What hast thou in the house?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 4:2 records that Elisha asked her what she had in the house.

questions.question: What was the only thing the woman had in her house?
options: A pot of oil
A jar of flour
A loaf of bread
A jug of wine
questions.correctAnswer: A pot of oil
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 4:2 states she had nothing but a pot of oil in the house.

questions.question: What did Elisha instruct the woman to do with vessels?
options: Borrow many empty vessels from neighbors
Sell the vessels she has
Fill the vessels with water
Break the vessels
questions.correctAnswer: Borrow many empty vessels from neighbors
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 4:3 says Elisha told her to borrow empty vessels from all her neighbors and not just a few.

questions.question: What was the woman to do after bringing the vessels inside?
options: Shut the door and pour oil into all the vessels
Fill them with water and leave the door open
Break some vessels and keep others
Sell the vessels to pay debts
questions.correctAnswer: Shut the door and pour oil into all the vessels
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 4:4 instructs her to shut the door and pour oil into all the vessels, setting aside those that become full.

questions.question: What happened when the vessels were all full?
options: The oil stopped flowing
The oil overflowed
The vessels broke
The creditor came
questions.correctAnswer: The oil stopped flowing
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 4:6 describes that after all vessels were full, the oil stayed and did not continue to flow.

questions.question: What did Elisha tell the woman to do after the vessels were filled with oil?
options: Sell the oil, pay thy debt, and live thou and thy children
Give the oil to the creditor
Use the oil for food
Keep the oil secretly
questions.correctAnswer: Sell the oil, pay thy debt, and live thou and thy children
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 4:7 says Elisha told her to sell the oil, pay her debt, and live on what remained.

questions.question: Where did Elisha visit when he met the great woman who offered him bread?
options: Shunem
Gilgal
Baalshalisha
Samaria
questions.correctAnswer: Shunem
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 4:8 states that Elisha passed to Shunem where the great woman constrained him to eat bread.

questions.question: What did the woman propose to make for Elisha on the wall?
options: A little chamber with a bed, table, stool, and candlestick
A large hall with many chairs
A garden shelter
A well with fresh water
questions.correctAnswer: A little chamber with a bed, table, stool, and candlestick
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 4:10 records her proposal to make a little chamber with furniture for Elisha to stay in.

questions.question: True or False: The woman who made the chamber for Elisha was called the Shunammite.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 4:12 shows Elisha told Gehazi to call the Shunammite woman, who is the same woman who made the chamber.

questions.question: True or False: Elisha offered to speak to the king or the captain of the host for the Shunammite woman.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 4:13 records Elisha asking Gehazi to ask the woman if she wanted him to speak for her to the king or captain of the host.

questions.question: True or False: The Shunammite woman asked Elisha to speak to the king to gain a royal position.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 4:13 shows she answered she dwells among her own people, declining the offer.

questions.question: True or False: Gehazi reported that the Shunammite woman had no child and her husband was old.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 4:14 states Gehazi told Elisha that she had no child and her husband was old.

medium.title: 2 Kings Chapter 4 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Kings Chapter 4 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What was Elisha's promise to the Shunammite woman about her future child?
options: She would have a son about this season
She would find a husband
She would receive great wealth
Her husband would be healed
questions.correctAnswer: She would have a son about this season
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 4:16, Elisha tells the woman she will embrace a son about this season. This promise is fulfilled as stated in 2 Kings 4:17.

questions.question: How did the Shunammite woman respond to Elisha's prophecy about having a son?
options: She doubted and said do not lie to me
She rejoiced immediately
She asked for a sign
She left without speaking
questions.correctAnswer: She doubted and said do not lie to me
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 4:16 records the woman saying, 'Nay, my lord, thou man of God, do not lie unto thine handmaid,' showing her initial disbelief in the prophecy.

questions.question: What happened to the child when he was grown and went out to his father to the reapers?
options: He complained of a headache and then died
He was injured by a tool
He was lost in the fields
He was taken ill but recovered
questions.correctAnswer: He complained of a headache and then died
questions.explanation: According to 2 Kings 4:19-20, the child said 'My head, my head' and later died while sitting on his mother's knees till noon.

questions.question: After the child's death, what did the Shunammite woman do with the body before seeking Elisha?
options: Laid him on Elisha's bed and shut the door
Buried him immediately
Called the village elders
Placed him on the kitchen floor
questions.correctAnswer: Laid him on Elisha's bed and shut the door
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 4:21 describes how the woman laid her dead son on the bed of the man of God and shut the door upon him before leaving to seek Elisha.

questions.question: How did the Shunammite woman show her determination to seek help from Elisha despite it not being a special day?
options: She said 'It shall be well' and rode quickly to him
She waited until the new moon
She asked for permission from the elders
She sent a servant alone
questions.correctAnswer: She said 'It shall be well' and rode quickly to him
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 4:23-24, when questioned why she went on an ordinary day, she assured 'It shall be well' and instructed her servant to ride quickly without slackening.

questions.question: What was Elisha's response when he saw the Shunammite woman coming to Mount Carmel?
options: He told Gehazi to run and inquire about her family
He immediately healed her child
He ignored her at first
He sent her away to wait
questions.correctAnswer: He told Gehazi to run and inquire about her family
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 4:25-26 records Elisha seeing her afar off and sending Gehazi to ask if all was well with her, her husband, and her child.

questions.question: What did the Shunammite woman do when she reached Elisha and was overcome with grief?
options: She caught him by the feet and expressed her sorrow
She fell to the ground without speaking
She asked for food and shelter
She immediately left in silence
questions.correctAnswer: She caught him by the feet and expressed her sorrow
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 4:27-28, she caught Elisha by the feet, and despite Gehazi’s attempt to push her away, Elisha told him to let her be because her soul was vexed.

questions.question: What instructions did Elisha give to Gehazi before going to the child?
options: Gird up thy loins, take my staff, do not greet anyone, and lay the staff on the child’s face
Bring food and water for the child
Pray at the city gates
Call the elders of the town
questions.correctAnswer: Gird up thy loins, take my staff, do not greet anyone, and lay the staff on the child’s face
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 4:29 instructs Gehazi to prepare himself, avoid greetings, and use Elisha’s staff on the child’s face as part of the healing process.

questions.question: What was the result when Gehazi laid Elisha’s staff on the child's face?
options: There was no response; the child did not awaken
The child sneezed immediately
The child opened his eyes
The child cried out loudly
questions.correctAnswer: There was no response; the child did not awaken
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 4:31 reveals Gehazi found no voice or hearing from the child after laying the staff on his face, indicating no immediate effect.

questions.question: How did Elisha finally revive the dead child?
options: By praying, laying on the child, and stretching himself upon him
By calling the elders to anoint him with oil
By ordering Gehazi to bring water
By fasting and praying for seven days
questions.correctAnswer: By praying, laying on the child, and stretching himself upon him
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 4:33-35 describes Elisha praying, laying on the child with his mouth, eyes, and hands, and stretching himself upon him until the child sneezed and opened his eyes.

questions.question: What does the Shunammite woman’s insistence in 2 Kings 4:30 teach us about faith and perseverance?
options: She would not leave Elisha, showing steadfast faith and trust
She abandoned hope and sought help elsewhere
She demanded a sign before following
She doubted Elisha’s power
questions.correctAnswer: She would not leave Elisha, showing steadfast faith and trust
questions.explanation: Her declaration in 2 Kings 4:30 to not leave Elisha 'as the LORD liveth' demonstrates her perseverance and trust in God's power through His prophet.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 4:26 promise will happen if the Shunammite woman follows Gehazi’s instructions and goes to Elisha?
options: She will find her family well and receive help
She will be turned away
Her child will remain dead
She will be asked to wait
questions.correctAnswer: She will find her family well and receive help
questions.explanation: Gehazi’s question and her response 'It is well' in 2 Kings 4:26 indicate an expectation of restoration and blessing upon her seeking Elisha, linking her obedience to receiving help.

questions.question: True or False: Gehazi tried to stop the Shunammite woman from clinging to Elisha because the man of God was ready to help her immediately.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 4:27 records Gehazi coming near to thrust her away, but Elisha said to let her alone because her soul was vexed and the LORD had hidden the matter from him, indicating Elisha was not yet aware and Gehazi’s intent was not tied to readiness to help.

questions.question: True or False: The Shunammite woman’s response to Elisha’s prophecy shows a biblical example of honest doubt and fear in the face of God’s promises.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Her words in 2 Kings 4:16, 'Nay, my lord, thou man of God, do not lie unto thine handmaid,' reflect her honest struggle with accepting the promise, illustrating biblical realism in faith.

questions.question: True or False: The Shunammite woman’s actions after her son’s death teach us about immediate grief and waiting passively for God’s timing.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 4:21-25 shows she acted promptly by laying the child on Elisha’s bed, seeking help immediately rather than passively waiting, demonstrating active faith and urgency.

hard.title: 2 Kings Chapter 4 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Kings Chapter 4.

questions.question: What was Gehazi instructed to do before laying Elisha's staff on the dead child's face?
options: Greet every man he met on the way
Avoid greeting anyone and answer no one
Sing a psalm on the way
Pray continuously
questions.correctAnswer: Avoid greeting anyone and answer no one
questions.explanation: Elisha told Gehazi not to greet anyone nor answer if greeted before laying the staff on the child's face (2 Kings 4:29). This symbolizes total focus and obedience in the miracle act, reflecting the seriousness of the prophet's mission. This parallels Jesus instructing silence before miracles in Mark 1:44.

questions.question: What significant event happened after Elisha stretched himself upon the child?
options: The child sneezed seven times and opened his eyes
The child immediately sat up and spoke
The child cried out loudly
The child remained still without any change
questions.correctAnswer: The child sneezed seven times and opened his eyes
questions.explanation: After Elisha stretched himself upon the child, the child sneezed seven times and opened his eyes, indicating his revival (2 Kings 4:35). The number seven often symbolizes completeness in Hebrew literature, showing the thoroughness of God's healing power, similar to Jesus healing the sick in the New Testament.

questions.question: What was the cause of the pottage being harmful to eat?
options: It contained wild gourds from a wild vine
It was undercooked
It was cursed by a prophet
It was mixed with poisonous herbs
questions.correctAnswer: It contained wild gourds from a wild vine
questions.explanation: The harmful pottage was caused by wild gourds unknowingly added from a wild vine (2 Kings 4:39-40). This reflects the cultural knowledge about toxic plants in the ancient Near East and shows God's provision through Elisha's intervention to make it safe (2 Kings 4:41).

questions.question: How did Elisha make the pottage safe to eat again?
options: He prayed over it
He added meal to the pot
He boiled it longer
He discarded the entire pot
questions.correctAnswer: He added meal to the pot
questions.explanation: Elisha cast meal into the pot and told them to pour it out for the people, after which it became safe to eat (2 Kings 4:41). This act shows a form of purification and foreshadows New Testament themes of bread and provision, as seen in John 6.

questions.question: What was Elisha's response when his servant doubted the sufficiency of twenty loaves for a hundred men?
options: He told him to give the loaves anyway because the LORD said they shall eat and have leftovers
He agreed and divided the loaves among only twenty men
He asked for more loaves to be brought
He performed a miracle to multiply the loaves
questions.correctAnswer: He told him to give the loaves anyway because the LORD said they shall eat and have leftovers
questions.explanation: Elisha insisted the servant give the bread to the people because the LORD promised they would eat and have leftovers, emphasizing divine provision (2 Kings 4:43). This echoes Jesus’s feeding miracles in the Gospels (e.g., Matthew 14:20).

questions.question: Which location is mentioned as the place where Elisha revived the Shunammite woman's son?
options: Shunem
Gilgal
Mount Carmel
Jericho
questions.correctAnswer: Shunem
questions.explanation: The child was laid on the bed of the man of God in Shunem, where he was revived by Elisha (2 Kings 4:32-36). Shunem is significant as the home of the woman who had provided hospitality to Elisha, establishing a theme of blessing for hospitality similar to Luke 10:38-42.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in the narrative of Elisha reviving the Shunammite’s son?
options: Chiasm
Parable
Allegory
Simile
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: The narrative uses chiasm, a literary structure where elements are presented and then mirrored in reverse order, seen in Elisha's actions of laying on the child and the child sneezing seven times (2 Kings 4:33-35). This emphasizes the completeness and divine order of the miracle, a common Hebrew literary technique.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word translated as 'staff' used in the account of Elisha’s miracle on the child?
options: A symbol of authority and God's power
A common walking stick
A weapon used in battle
A measuring rod
questions.correctAnswer: A symbol of authority and God's power
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'staff' (מַטֶּה, matteh) often symbolizes authority and God's power through the prophet, as shown when Gehazi uses it in the miracle (2 Kings 4:29). This typology echoes Moses’s staff in Exodus as a divine instrument.

questions.question: How did the Shunammite woman react when Elisha told her she would have a son?
options: She said, 'Nay, my lord, thou man of God, do not lie unto thine handmaid'
She rejoiced and praised the LORD immediately
She asked for a sign to confirm
She doubted silently without speaking
questions.correctAnswer: She said, 'Nay, my lord, thou man of God, do not lie unto thine handmaid'
questions.explanation: She expressed disbelief and pleaded for truth, reflecting human doubt in divine promises (2 Kings 4:16). This honest response highlights the realism in prophetic narratives and is similar to Hannah's initial barrenness and prayer in 1 Samuel 1.

questions.question: True or False: Elisha immediately followed Gehazi after he laid the staff on the child's face.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Elisha followed Gehazi because the staff did not revive the child, showing Elisha's personal involvement and the necessity of the prophet's presence (2 Kings 4:31-32). This demonstrates the importance of prophetic authority.

questions.question: True or False: The Shunammite woman only asked for Elisha to speak to the king or captain on her behalf.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: She declined any special favor from the king or captain, saying she dwelt among her own people (2 Kings 4:13). This shows humility and contentment, contrasting many biblical figures who sought royal favor.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of God providing bread miraculously as seen in 2 Kings 4:42-44?
options: Exodus 16 (Manna in the wilderness)
Genesis 1 (Creation of food)
Leviticus 11 (Dietary laws)
Numbers 13 (Spies in Canaan)
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 16 (Manna in the wilderness)
questions.explanation: The miraculous provision of bread in 2 Kings 4:42-44 echoes Exodus 16 where God provides manna to the Israelites in the wilderness. Both demonstrate God's sustaining power during times of need.

questions.question: How does the revival of the Shunammite’s son in 2 Kings 4 relate typologically to New Testament resurrection accounts?
options: It prefigures Jesus raising the dead, showing God's power over death
It is unrelated to New Testament events
It only symbolizes physical healing, not resurrection
It was a unique event with no typology
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures Jesus raising the dead, showing God's power over death
questions.explanation: The raising of the child (2 Kings 4:32-37) prefigures Jesus raising Lazarus and others, highlighting God's authority over death and foreshadowing resurrection hope (John 11).

questions.question: What cultural practice is reflected in the Shunammite woman laying her dead son on Elisha’s bed and shutting the door before going out to seek help?
options: Respect for the prophet’s space and privacy
A ritual to ward off evil spirits
A funerary custom of the time
A sign of mourning in public
questions.correctAnswer: Respect for the prophet’s space and privacy
questions.explanation: Laying the child on Elisha's bed and shutting the door (2 Kings 4:21) shows respect for the prophet's personal space and possibly an act of faith, emphasizing the sacredness of the prophet's house in Israelite culture.

questions.question: Which event in the New Testament best parallels the theme of Elisha’s miraculous provision and healing in this chapter?
options: Jesus feeding the 5,000 and healing the sick
The Pentecost outpouring
Paul’s missionary journeys
The Transfiguration
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus feeding the 5,000 and healing the sick
questions.explanation: Elisha’s miracles of provision and healing (2 Kings 4) foreshadow Jesus’ ministry of feeding the multitudes and healing diseases, emphasizing God's compassion and power (Matthew 14:13-21).

theological.title: 2 Kings Chapter 4 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Kings Chapter 4 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine is illustrated by Elisha's instruction to the widow to borrow many empty vessels and pour her single pot of oil into them until they were all full?
options: The doctrine of God's providential provision
The doctrine of original sin
The doctrine of predestination
The doctrine of justification by faith alone
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of God's providential provision
questions.explanation: Elisha's instructions and the miraculous multiplication of oil show God's providential care and provision for His people in times of need, as seen in 2 Kings 4:3-6. This demonstrates God's attribute of providence, ensuring His people are cared for according to His purposes (cf. Philippians 4:19).

questions.question: Which attribute of God is demonstrated when Elisha prays and the dead child is revived in 2 Kings 4?
options: God's omnipotence
God's justice
God's wrath
God's patience
questions.correctAnswer: God's omnipotence
questions.explanation: Elisha's prayer and the child's revival (2 Kings 4:33-35) demonstrate God's omnipotence over life and death, showing that God has power to give life and restore the dead, foreshadowing Christ's resurrection power (John 11:43-44).

questions.question: How does the narrative of the Shunammite woman providing a room for Elisha (2 Kings 4:8-10) connect to the broader redemptive story of Scripture?
options: It foreshadows Christ's hospitality and the establishment of the Church as a place of refuge
It reveals the fallenness of humanity
It shows the failure of Israel's kings
It teaches the importance of temple worship
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows Christ's hospitality and the establishment of the Church as a place of refuge
questions.explanation: The Shunammite woman's care for Elisha (a prophet of God) by preparing a special room (2 Kings 4:8-10) prefigures Christ's welcoming of people and the Church becoming a spiritual refuge, demonstrating the biblical theme of hospitality and God's presence among His people (Hebrews 13:2).

questions.question: Considering 2 Kings 4:38-41, what theological truth is taught through the episode of the poisonous pottage that Elisha makes safe by adding meal?
options: God's power to sanctify and preserve His people
The inevitability of death
The judgment of God on sin
The importance of dietary laws
questions.correctAnswer: God's power to sanctify and preserve His people
questions.explanation: When Elisha miraculously neutralizes the deadly pottage (2 Kings 4:40-41), it illustrates God's protective power to preserve His people from harm, symbolizing His sanctifying work and sustaining grace (Psalm 91:3-4).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight is conveyed by the widow's faith in verses 2-7 and Elisha's prophecy of a son to the Shunammite woman in verses 16-17?
options: Both episodes reveal God's covenant faithfulness and the role of faith in God's miraculous provision
They show that God only helps prophets' families
They emphasize human effort over divine intervention
They teach that blessings are earned by works
questions.correctAnswer: Both episodes reveal God's covenant faithfulness and the role of faith in God's miraculous provision
questions.explanation: The widow's trust to gather vessels for the oil (2 Kings 4:2-7) and the Shunammite woman's conception after Elisha's prophecy (2 Kings 4:16-17) together show God's faithfulness to His covenant promises and the necessity of faith to receive His miraculous provision (Hebrews 11:6).

questions.question: How does the resurrection of the Shunammite woman's son (2 Kings 4:33-36) typologically point to Christ's resurrection?
options: It prefigures Christ's power to overcome death and bring eternal life
It symbolizes the resurrection of Israel
It represents the resurrection of all prophets
It foreshadows the destruction of death
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures Christ's power to overcome death and bring eternal life
questions.explanation: The raising of the child by Elisha (2 Kings 4:33-36) serves as a type of Christ's resurrection power, revealing God's ultimate authority over death through the Messiah (1 Corinthians 15:20-22).

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 4:1-7 reveal about human sin and divine grace in the context of the widow's predicament?
options: Human sin results in debt and bondage, but divine grace provides deliverance
Human sin is irrelevant to God's actions
Divine grace always removes human responsibility
Debt is a blessing from God
questions.correctAnswer: Human sin results in debt and bondage, but divine grace provides deliverance
questions.explanation: The widow's fear of losing her sons to slavery due to debt (2 Kings 4:1) reflects the consequences of sin and brokenness, yet God's grace through Elisha's miracle delivers her family from bondage, displaying God's redemptive mercy (Romans 6:23).

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 4:44, what does the leftover food after feeding many people teach about God's nature?
options: God is abundantly generous and able to provide beyond human limitations
God is limited by natural resources
God punishes those who doubt
God only provides for the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: God is abundantly generous and able to provide beyond human limitations
questions.explanation: The miracle of feeding many with barley loaves and having leftovers (2 Kings 4:44) reveals God's abundant generosity and supernatural provision, reflecting His grace that exceeds human expectations (John 6:11-13).

questions.question: What theological significance does the Shunammite woman's persistence in seeking Elisha's help for her dead son (2 Kings 4:27-30) reveal?
options: It teaches the importance of faith and perseverance in prayer
It shows that God is indifferent to human suffering
It implies that miracles are guaranteed on demand
It suggests that only prophets can perform miracles
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches the importance of faith and perseverance in prayer
questions.explanation: The woman's refusal to leave Elisha (2 Kings 4:30) demonstrates persistent faith and trust in God's power to intervene, encouraging believers to persevere in prayer despite difficulties (Luke 18:1-8).

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by Elisha's instruction to Gehazi not to greet anyone and to lay his staff on the dead child’s face (2 Kings 4:29)?
options: The doctrine of spiritual authority and obedience
The doctrine of salvation by works
The doctrine of human autonomy
The doctrine of predestination
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of spiritual authority and obedience
questions.explanation: Elisha's command to Gehazi (2 Kings 4:29) highlights the necessity of obedience to God's instructions and the exercise of spiritual authority through prophetic action, reflecting God's sovereign power working through His servants (Hebrews 13:17).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that miracles in Scripture are exaggerated stories to inspire faith. What does 2 Kings 4:38-41 actually teach about God's involvement with His people?
options: God actively intervenes in physical realities to protect and sustain His people
Miracles are merely symbolic stories
God is distant and uninvolved
Nature operates independently of God
questions.correctAnswer: God actively intervenes in physical realities to protect and sustain His people
questions.explanation: The neutralization of poisonous pottage (2 Kings 4:38-41) affirms God's active and personal involvement in the lives of His people, demonstrating His power over creation and care for human well-being, validating the reality of biblical miracles (Acts 14:8-10).

questions.question: What does the account of the Shunammite woman’s barrenness and subsequent conception (2 Kings 4:14-17) teach about God's sovereign work in salvation history?
options: God can bring life and blessing out of apparent impossibility according to His sovereign will
Human effort is the primary cause of blessing
Barrenness is a curse that cannot be reversed
God is limited by human age and condition
questions.correctAnswer: God can bring life and blessing out of apparent impossibility according to His sovereign will
questions.explanation: The miraculous conception of a son to an old couple (2 Kings 4:14-17) shows God's sovereign ability to bring about new life and blessings contrary to natural circumstances, echoing divine promises of restoration and hope (Genesis 18:14).

questions.question: What combined teaching do 2 Kings 4:22-26 and 2 Kings 4:33-36 convey about God's power and human response in times of crisis?
options: God's power to heal and restore invites persistent faith and active seeking
God passively allows suffering without intervention
Human efforts alone can resolve crises
Miracles happen only when conditions are perfect
questions.correctAnswer: God's power to heal and restore invites persistent faith and active seeking
questions.explanation: The Shunammite woman’s urgent journey to Elisha (2 Kings 4:22-26) and the subsequent resurrection of her son (2 Kings 4:33-36) together teach that God's healing power responds to persistent faith and active pursuit, encouraging believers to trust and seek Him in difficulties (James 5:15-16).

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed by Elisha’s willingness to pray and physically lay upon the dead child (2 Kings 4:33-34)?
options: God's compassion and relational nature
God's impassibility
God's wrathful judgment
God's aloofness
questions.correctAnswer: God's compassion and relational nature
questions.explanation: Elisha's intimate actions in praying and laying on the child (2 Kings 4:33-34) reveal God's compassionate character and His relational engagement with humanity, demonstrating that God deeply cares about human suffering (Psalm 34:18).

questions.question: What does the instruction to set aside that which is full when pouring oil into vessels (2 Kings 4:4) symbolize theologically?
options: God’s abundant blessings are meant to be preserved and shared
Material wealth is the ultimate goal
Faith requires self-sufficiency
Blessings are limited and must be hoarded
questions.correctAnswer: God’s abundant blessings are meant to be preserved and shared
questions.explanation: The command to set aside full vessels (2 Kings 4:4) symbolizes the responsible stewardship of God's blessings, emphasizing that divine provision is abundant and intended for preservation and sharing with others (2 Corinthians 9:10-11).
